note: RAM guard defaults. Merge order: this file < ~/.claude/team/ram-guard.json (user) < <project>/.claude/team/ram-guard.json (project). The user file may change anything. The project file may only make things stricter: it can raise a threshold (never above the user's project_max_mb), add kinds, and add patterns or tools to a kind; 'enabled', lowering a threshold and project_max_mb in it are ignored with a warning. A user kind of the same name replaces a field of this file (min_free_mb, patterns, tools, enabled, hook_if). 'enabled': false at the top level switches the whole guard off, per kind that kind. A kind needs 'min_free_mb' (a number above 0) and either 'tools' containing Agent/Task (matches every subagent spawn; patterns are ignored for those tools), or 'patterns' (regular expressions, case-insensitive, 200 ms match timeout, matched against the Bash/PowerShell command; 'tools' then defaults to Bash and PowerShell; a shell kind without a valid pattern is skipped). The guard blocks a new call when the free physical memory (available memory: free plus cache that can be dropped) is below 'min_free_mb' of the matching kind (the highest one if several match). It never kills anything. 'hook_if': command globs used only by the installer to start the hook for Bash/PowerShell only when a command matches (Bash(claude *) etc.); a user kind with patterns but no hook_if, or 'scan_all_commands': true in the user file, makes the installer register the hook for every shell command instead (slower). Re-run install.ps1 after changing hook_if.
